title: How World Liberty insiders took money out
summary: The documented record supports most of the brief. Trump-owned DT Marks DEFI is entitled to 75% of WLF's net revenue, including token-sale proceeds. Trump disclosed about $57M from WLF for 2024 and about $800M for 2025. Steve Witkoff reported about $107M of 2025 income from a WLF-linked holding company while the White House says he has divested, though no buyer or certificate has been shown. WLF borrowed about $75M of stablecoins on Dolomite against about 5B WLFI as the token hit record lows. Sun's wallet and 271 others were frozen, WLF promoted the $SPSC memecoin, and WLFI fell about 80-85% from its $0.33 peak. Three points need correction or remain open: the borrower was WLF's own treasury, not individual insiders; no source puts a dollar figure on retail losses; and StringZ Holding's reported Tahnoon backing rests on a single WSJ report citing anonymous sources, which the OCC record does not confirm.

sub_claims.statement: DT Marks DEFI LLC is entitled to 75% of WLF's net token-sale and protocol revenue.
sub_claims.finding: The October 2024 Gold Paper gives DT Marks DEFI 22.5B WLFI and 75% of 'net protocol revenues'. These cover revenue from any source, including token-sale proceeds and fees, after a $30M reserve and agreed expenses. The other 25% goes to Axiom Management Group, owned by Herro and Folkman. On the $550M raised, Decrypt estimated about $390M for Trump-side entities, though one analyst disputes that reading. This entitlement is separate from DT Marks DEFI's equity in WLF Holdco, which was reported at about 60%, then 40%, then 38.25%.

The 2024 OGE filing, released June 2025, shows about $57.35M from WLF token sales ($57.7M per Bloomberg Tax). The 2025 filing, released June 30, 2026, shows about $800M: more than $520M from token sales and more than $250M from selling interests in the business. The 22.5B-token stake was valued at about $1.3B. These are revenue figures, not profit.

sub_claims.statement: Steve Witkoff received about $107M of 2025 income from his WLF-linked holding company.
sub_claims.finding: His 2025 OGE disclosure, reported by ABC in September 2026 from a watchdog's copy, shows nearly $107M from a WLF-affiliated holding company, up from $34M in 2024. One outlet splits it into about $69M cash and $38M in digital assets. The filing does not show how much came from WLF itself and had not been certified. His 2025 new-entrant report listed WC Digital Fi LLC, which WLF's documents describe as an affiliate of Witkoff and his family.

sub_claims.statement: Witkoff's divestment from WLF is disputed.
sub_claims.finding: WLF said in May 2025 that he was 'in the process' of divesting. Bloomberg (Sept 2025) and Senate Democrats (Oct 2025) said he still held WLF assets. The White House said in February 2026 that he had divested, and in September 2026 that he had 'fully divested'. No divestiture certificate, buyer or price has been published, so whether the divestment is complete cannot be verified.

sub_claims.statement: WLF insiders borrowed stablecoins against about 5B WLFI tokens as the price hit lows.
sub_claims.finding: WLF-controlled treasury or multisig wallets, not individual insiders, pledged about 5B WLFI on Dolomite and borrowed about $75M (about 65.4M USD1 plus 10.3M USDC). More than $40M was sent to Coinbase Prime, and the USD1 pool was drained to about 93-100% utilization. Dolomite's co-founder Corey Caplan is a WLF adviser. WLFI fell 12-19% to then-record lows of about $0.077-0.080, erasing about $427M of market value. WLF called the concern 'FUD' and said it repaid $25M by April 11, leaving about $50M. The larger $150M and $261M estimates are unverified. In August 2026 CryptoSlate reported a 112.6M USD1 position near liquidation.

sub_claims.statement: WLF froze the tokens of Justin Sun and other holders.
sub_claims.finding: WLF blacklisted Sun's address around Sept 4-5, 2025, after about $9M of WLFI moved, freezing about 540-600M unlocked tokens plus a reported 2.4B locked tokens. WLF said 272 wallets were frozen in total, mostly over phishing. In November 2025 it burned and reallocated about 166.7M WLFI to holders who passed new KYC checks. Sun was still frozen in December 2025, with his stake down more than $60M. A vesting vote in May 2026 locked 17B early-supporter tokens for two years. Sun said he could not vote because his tokens were frozen.

On Nov 24, 2025, WLF said it would invest in $SPSC, a Solana memecoin named after Chase Herro's 'shit in a can' rant and paired with USD1. It rose 130-143%, to a market cap of about $6.8M. Arkham data showed WLF had not yet bought any. No reliable figure exists for a later crash.

sub_claims.statement: WLFI price history and retail losses.
sub_claims.finding: Presale prices were $0.015 and $0.05. The token peaked at about $0.33 on Sept 1, 2025, its first trading day. It hit lows of about $0.077 in April 2026 and about $0.05 in early May 2026, and traded around $0.05-0.06 through October 2026, down about 80-85% from the peak. Open-market buyers are deep underwater and most early-supporter tokens are still locked. No source puts a dollar figure on WLFI retail losses.

The OCC's Aug 14, 2026 conditional charter decision names StringZ Holding RSC (DE) LLC as a passive investor in WLTC Holdings, without naming its owner or stake size. The WSJ (Aug 27, 2026), citing anonymous sources, reported that a group linked to Tahnoon bin Zayed is behind StringZ, which holds 49%, and that a Trump-family entity holds about 38%. No primary document confirms this, and StringZ's link to Aryam Investment 1 is unknown.

corrections: The brief says 'WLF insiders' borrowed. The reporting shows WLF's own treasury or multisig wallets borrowed on Dolomite, and no personal borrowing by Trump or Witkoff family members is documented. Loan size: about $75M per CoinDesk; the $150M and $261M estimates are unverified.
'75% of net revenue' is the Gold Paper revenue entitlement. DT Marks DEFI's equity stake in WLF Holdco is now reported at about 38.25%.
Witkoff's about $107M came from a WLF-linked holding company, and the filing does not show how much came from WLF itself.
Entity id note: C04 uses dt-marks-defi-llc and C13 uses dt-marks-defi for the same company. This file uses dt-marks-defi-llc.
denials_and_context: WLF says the freezes protect users from phishing, calls concerns about the Dolomite loan 'FUD' because the position is overcollateralized, and calls Sun's allegations baseless.
The White House (Anna Kelly, David Warrington) says Witkoff has fully divested and recuses from matters affecting his interests.
The OCC says career staff reviewed the WLF trust charter, and says the major shareholders, including StringZ, signed passivity commitments.
'Extraction' is a characterization. The money flows are documented, but no regulator or court has found wrongdoing, and the SEC has opened no probe (see C13).
Fetch limits: Fortune, CoinDesk and the ABC affiliate pages could not be fetched here, and the WSJ is paywalled. Findings rely on search-result text cross-checked across outlets.

leads.why_connected: A direct extraction route alongside the 75% revenue share: WLF sold tokens while retail presale holders could not sell.

leads.why_connected: The Dolomite borrowing was still near liquidation in August 2026, just as the OCC was approving WLF's trust bank. The current balance needs checking.

leads.why_connected: WLF unilaterally burned and reissued holders' tokens. The governance and legal basis is unexamined.
